column7: ClassifyMachineToken read a machine credential unlocked and persisted it through UpdateMachineIdentityCredential, a bare GORM Save of the WHOLE row -- so a RevokeMachineToken that committed on another replica between the read and the write was silently reverted (revoked=false written back), and the revoked, possibly leaked token authenticated again with nothing in the audit trail showing the un-revoke. Reachable over gRPC/HTTP with roles.assign on the project. Fixed by replacing the full-row primitive OUTRIGHT with SetMachineIdentityCredentialClassification, a conditional column-scoped UPDATE of classification alone gated on the value the caller read; machine_identity_credentials now has no full-row writer at all (revoked moves only via RevokeMachineIdentityCredential's UpdateColumn, last_used_at only via TouchMachineIdentityCredential). Red on real Postgres before the fix: the revoked token re-authenticated (ValidateMachineToken returned no error). Found by C-GUARD-3 guard 1
